KHASI AT THE STATE LEVEL AND THE 
SAHITYAAKADEMI

ByH.W.Sten

Introduction

I got a letter from our General secretary (Mr. S.S. Majaw) that I should 
speak on ‘ Awareness on the importance of Khasi Language' . He also gave me 
guideline that my scope is specially the position of Khasi in Meghala\a and the 
Sahitya Akademi I propose to be brief, leaving the details to Mr. Sylvanus Lamare 
who is presently working on ‘'Linguistic Awareness Among the Khasis”.

In Meghalaya

History is independent of Linguistics and Literature Academic decorum 
should be observed. One from another discipline should refrain himself (if he 
were not a fool) from intrusion into somebody else’s territory.

As far as my poor information guides me, Khasi was in use m offices since 
the 1 9th century Previously we had only one district, the United Khasi and Jaintia 
Hills. We have now four district as we multiplied ourselves in term of population. 
The increase in population and the number of district from one to four has not 
changed the status of Khasi. In fact, the number of schools also has increased as 
has the number of Christian churches and parishes We all used Khasi in churches 
and in schools

When we refer to schools we should not claim that the first school in our 
state was opened around Sohra because David Scott opened the first school in our 
state in 1826, and that was in the Garo Hills

The supreme body in our state is the Assembly permits any member* to 
speak in Khasi. Let us read that rule, we shall see how we as electors did to our 
languages : Khasi and Garo.

28. The business of the Assembly shall be translated into English:-

Provided that a member may address the Assembly in his mother longlie^ 
only when he makes over and the Secretary a copy of the English vmion of

[ 2 ]

intended speech atjenst half an hour before the commencement of the sitting on 
which he proposes to speak and also circulates such copies to the members at his 
own initiative immediately before he delivers his speech on the floor of the House.

Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business 
in Meghalaya Legislative Assembly (rpt 1987).

In the absence of the nouns Khasi and Garo in the rule, I must admit that I 
take shelter in the phrase “mother tongue” which is flexible enough to include any 
“tongue” a member of the Assembly speaks; but the condition is also clear. The 
English translation must be submitted to the Assembly.

Following what the Government of Assam did, our state government 
continued to give financial assistance to Khasi authors. Whether or not the 
assistance was sufficient, is a matter of interpretation. To witness that I, too, 
received such assistance once

The state literary award was also instituted. The amount has increased 
lately. The paucity of standard works submitted for scrutiny could possibly be that 
most authors felt, as Sister Philomena Kharakor once said, that it was like 
begging for the convetous award, A change of mind on the part of the government 
and the authors will make the programme a success.

As a step to advance the progress of the language and literatures of the 
Khasis and the Garos, the state government, vide Notification No. MAC 23/88/78 
dated the 4th August 1995, constituted the State Akademi fpr Literature, Fine 
Arts and Performing Arts. If I understand the wordings of the notification as do 
Others, I may perhaps maintain that the Government of Meghalaya recognizes not 
only Khasi but also the Khasi Authors’ Society.

In these days when reason counts, it may be invoked here. The state 
government sanctioned Rs. 25,900/- as grant to the Khasi Authors’ Society this 
year There might have been reasons, valid or invalid, for non-extending of 
helpihg hands to the Society for a few years.

What the Government of Meghalaya has not done also must be stated. It 
has not brought a bill to make Khasi and Garo associate official languages of the 
state. Vertical planning as provided by Article 345 of the Constitution of India is 
to be prefested as literal planning as (uovtded by Article 347 mhy result in law 
and order problem.

[31

In whatever way we want the Government of Meghataya to promote Khasi 
language and literature, the users of the langiu^e ooitkl better judges than 1 am.

In the Sahitya Akademi

The sahitya Akademi was inaugurated on the 12th March 1954 and 
registered under the Societies Registration Act, I860 on the 7th January 1956. 
I have no record to conjecture that the Akademi ever heard about Khasi prior to 
the creation of Meghalaya. It was only on the I6th February 1973 when Dr. R.S. 
Lyngdoh, then member representing Meghalaya moved a resolution in the 
General Council that the Executive Board deputed a fact finding conunittee to 
Shillong I have also no other records to prove that Meghalaya representatives 
ever attempted to convince the Akademi by their deliberations or resolutions in 
pursuance of the noble effort of the late Professor tyngdoh.

When the^asi Authors’ Society was organized in 1979, the matter was 
taken up rather vigorously Another experts’ committee visited Shillong and Sohra 
and submitted its unfavourable report finding faults with trivial matters. The Khasi 
Authors’ Society under different leadership has been in touch with the Sahitya 
Akademi. In a particular year the KAS demanded that a particular member be 
considered for nomination by the Government of Meghalaya to the Akademi. 
That particular member was nominated by the Akademi itself This will not 
happen again; because the Akademi has decided that universities will be electoral 
colleges.

In theory, it appears to me that the Akademi since 1994, the year four 
scholars from Shillong were invited to participate in the translation workshop in 
collaboration with the ABILAC of Assam. Two progranunes were held in town 
since then, though the Khasi Authors’ Society was not involved. The pieces 
translated in the workshop by Mrs Streamlet Dkhar, M.A., M..Phil.^ Ph.D.,
